description: NaAlGeP₂SO₁₂ crystallizes in the monoclinic Cc space group. Na is bonded in a hexagonal planar geometry to six O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.42-2.50 Å. Al is bonded to six O atoms to form AlO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent SO₄ tetrahedra and corners with four PO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Al-O bond distances ranging from 1.80-2.00 Å. Ge is bonded to six O atoms to form GeO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent SO₄ tetrahedra and corners with four PO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of Ge-O bond distances ranging from 1.84-1.99 Å. There are two inequivalent P sites. In the first P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent AlO₆ octahedra and corners with two equivalent GeO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 28-35°. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.51-1.56 Å. In the second P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent AlO₆ octahedra and corners with two equivalent GeO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 24-37°. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.51-1.57 Å. S is bonded to four O atoms to form SO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent AlO₆ octahedra and corners with two equivalent GeO₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 29-36°. There are two shorter (1.46 Å) and two longer (1.50 Å) S-O bond lengths. There are twelve inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a bent 150 degrees geometry to one Al and one S atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Ge, and one P atom. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one Al, and one P atom. In the eighth O site, O is bonded in a bent 150 degrees geometry to one Ge and one P atom. In the ninth O site, O is bonded in a bent 150 degrees geometry to one Ge and one S atom. In the tenth O site, O is bonded in a bent 150 degrees geometry to one Ge and one P atom.
